method_limits: a null sentinel is read off the AST only: None / False / '' / () / [] / {} / set() / frozenset() / dict() / list() / tuple(). A sentinel computed by a helper (``NULL = _null()``) is outside this scan and is never published as absent
the counter must be a Name tested against a single comparison: a test hidden behind ``not``, ``all(...)`` or a helper predicate is outside this scan

a name tested against a constant is a *depth counter* only when it is named like one (depth/level/lvl/ply/hop) or when it is bumped by one into a call of the same function; every other such test is a bar index or a length guard and is counted in rejected_counter_tests rather than dropped silently (``elig(prices, i)`` testing ``i < MIN_BARS`` is the shape this rejects)

``distinguishable`` means the call site compares the result against a value that is not the same null spelling; a site that only tests ``is None`` cannot separate the cap from the absence, so it is published under D_SAME_SENTINEL rather than as a reader

an arm is published dead only when the counter reaches the function purely by being forwarded (never assigned in the body), the function carries no recursive call, the cap is an int constant, and every counter value a call site can supply -- a literal argument or a literal default when the argument is omitted -- is below the cap. A counter assigned in the body is a loop counter that can reach the cap from any call, and a non-literal value keeps the arm alive

a call site decides an arm only when the call and the definition live in the same module, or when the calling module imports the defining module's stem -- anything else is a same-name collision and is published as unattributed_same_name_calls (``main`` alone collides with over a thousand ``sys.exit(main())`` sites), never as a reader
nothing is executed and no source is rewritten
sources_read is a snapshot of a live tree that other lanes write to; it is published but not gated, while every verdict class is re-derived
